title: Construction and Validation of a Machine Learning-Based Risk Prediction Model for Recurrent Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding in Patients with Liver Cirrhosis: A Prospective Study
summary: A machine-learning risk model for recurrent upper-GI bleeding in cirrhosis was assessed in a prospective development cohort and an independent external cohort. The selected logistic model achieved external AUC 0.827 (95% CI 0.747–0.907). This supports prediction in the studied cohorts; it does not establish improved outcomes or causal effects.
ai_technology: Four machine-learning classifiers; logistic regression was selected
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: A prospective 505-patient development cohort and an independent 148-patient external cohort were used to predict six-month recurrent upper-GI bleeding in cirrhosis. The selected logistic model had external AUC 0.827 (95% CI 0.747–0.907), with decision-curve analysis.
evidence.unknown: No impact trial or evidence of improved patient outcomes; findings are bounded to the studied cohorts and setting.
evidence.ai_role: Classifiers estimated individual recurrence risk from patient predictors.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
